homologation_count.label: 200 street units
homologation_count.blurb: Detroit must sell this many street coupes before the race body is legal.

choices.label: 200 street units
choices.blurb: A short street run. Detroit can homologate wilder coupes.

choices.label: 500 street units
choices.blurb: The late-sixties count. A real production line, not a handful.

choices.label: Per-dealership count
choices.blurb: Each dealer takes one. Superbird-era paperwork.

wheelbase_class.label: 110-inch downsized
wheelbase_class.blurb: The Cup car's wheelbase. Downsizing in 1981 made aero the war.

choices.label: 110-inch downsized
choices.blurb: The 1981 cut. Aero owns the big tracks.

choices.label: 115-inch intermediates
choices.blurb: Grand National wheelbase. Mechanical grip, less aero war.

choices.label: Mixed class
choices.blurb: Shops may run 110 or 115. Packing gets messy.

aero_specials.label: Aero specials banned
aero_specials.blurb: Winged cars and long noses. Homologate-to-run lets Detroit field them only after the street count is sold.

choices.label: Aero specials banned

choices.blurb: Specials are legal only if Detroit sells the street count.

choices.label: Aero specials legal
choices.blurb: Wings and long noses run if a factory will badge them.

inbox.subject: Welcome to Northstar Capital Stock Car Series
inbox.body:
Commissioner,

You run Northstar Capital Stock Car Series. You do not drive.

Television and naming rights pay the bills. Owners want wins. Drivers want a fair garage. The board wants a league that still exists next year.

Open every section on the left. Mail is your inbox. When the checklist is done, Advance runs the next week.

Python still simulates the races. This office is where you sit.
